price_stale_note: CBD.NZ was delisted from the NZX Main Board on 17 December 2024. The last traded price of NZ$0.098 is a frozen, non-transactable historical artifact echoed by Yahoo Finance from that final trading session - there has been no trading for approximately 20 months and no functioning secondary market exists. It is retained here only as the pipeline's required current_price field; it is NOT a live market quote and upside/downside figures computed against it are not economically meaningful (they are reported as -100% by construction, not because -100% was derived from a discount rate).
model_note: Cannasouth Limited is NOT a going-concern operating company and this is NOT a DCF candidate. A discounted-cash-flow model requires a repeatable, positive future cash flow stream to project and a terminal value to capitalize; Cannasouth has neither. It was placed into voluntary administration 28-Mar-2024, entered a Deed of Company Arrangement Jun-2024, was delisted from the NZX Main Board 17-Dec-2024, and was placed into RECEIVERSHIP 22-May-2025 (Kevin Davies, Principle Insolvency), with the receiver publicly stating liquidation is the expected outcome. In Feb-2026 the receiver sold the operating subsidiaries (Cannasouth Cultivation, Eqalis Group) to Marshall Road Holdings for NZ$4.7 million - proceeds explicitly reported as INSUFFICIENT to fully repay the ~NZ$2.53 million owed to secured GSA noteholders, before unsecured creditors (~NZ$0.109 million) or ordinary shareholders are considered at all. Historical FCF was deeply negative every year on record (FY2022 -NZ$5.70m, FY2021 -NZ$3.43m) with no audited accounts filed since FY2022. This model instead runs a creditor-priority liquidation waterfall on the realised/estimated asset pool, which is the only analytically honest way to value equity in an insolvent, receivership-controlled entity with a confirmed secured-creditor shortfall.

inputs.shares_outstanding_note: FY2022 weighted-average shares outstanding (140,435,616), the last audited figure on record (no FY2023+ audited accounts were ever filed). Approximately NZ$30 million of shareholder capital was raised and ultimately destroyed across the company's listed life (IPO Jun-2019 through delisting Dec-2024).
inputs.net_debt_note: Not meaningful in the conventional DCF sense - see waterfall below. The FY2022 balance sheet (last audited) showed total debt of NZ$3.672m and cash of NZ$1.912m, but those figures are now moot: the operating subsidiaries and their associated assets/liabilities have been sold out of receivership, and the only currently disclosed creditor figures are the receiver's own: ~NZ$2.53m secured GSA notes and ~NZ$0.109m unsecured.
inputs.last_fcf_note: Deliberately omitted. There is no repeatable free cash flow to project - historical FCF was deeply negative every year on record (FY2022 -NZ$5.70m, FY2021 -NZ$3.43m), the operating subsidiaries have been sold out of the listed entity entirely, and the receiver has stated liquidation is the expected outcome. Projecting a growth path from a negative, now non-existent cash flow base would be fabricating a business that no longer exists inside CBD.NZ.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2022 (last audited) free cash flow, NZ$ millions, shown for historical disclosure only - see historical_growth below for the full negative FCF/loss record leading into the 2024 collapse.
inputs.sbc_source: Metrics.csv StockBasedComp column, FY2022 (NZ$0.078m). Immaterial and not adjusted for further - the company has no going-concern operations to project SBC against.
inputs.units: millions except waterfall line items which are stated in absolute NZD for precision

waterfall.gross_realisations_note: Confirmed: Feb-2026 sale of operating subsidiaries Cannasouth Cultivation and Eqalis Group to Marshall Road Holdings for NZ$4.7 million. No further material asset recoveries are disclosed; liquidators of another part of the group were reported to be disputing certain asset sales and related-party loans, a genuinely uncertain and currently unquantified contingency handled only in the bull scenario below.
waterfall.receivership_liquidation_costs_note: Not separately disclosed by the receiver in the sources reviewed. Assumed range of NZ$0.6-1.5m (point estimate NZ$1.0m) for receivers' and liquidators' fees, legal costs and administrative wind-down costs, consistent with the scale of a NZ SME receivership/liquidation of this asset size and duration (receivership opened 22-May-2025, asset sale completed Feb-2026, liquidation process ongoing). This assumption is a material driver of the noteholder shortfall shown below and is disclosed explicitly rather than netted invisibly into the sale proceeds.
waterfall.secured_gsa_noteholders_note: Per the receiver's first report (Jul-2025) via the NZ Companies Office: GSA (secured, General Security Agreement) noteholders owed approximately NZ$2.53 million. The receiver reported the Feb-2026 subsidiary sale proceeds as INSUFFICIENT to repay this in full - i.e. there is a shortfall at the very top of the creditor waterfall before any junior claim (preferential, unsecured, or equity) is even reached.
waterfall.preferential_creditors_note: Employee entitlements and IRD/GST/PAYE preferential claims are not separately quantified in disclosed reporting. Given the secured creditor shortfall already exists before reaching this tier, any preferential claim only widens the gap further; treated as NZ$0 realised/unquantified here for conservatism on the cost side (i.e. NOT assumed away - simply already irrelevant to the equity outcome given the shortfall above it).
waterfall.unsecured_creditors_note: Per the receiver's first report (Jul-2025): unsecured creditors owed a further approximately NZ$109,000. Ranks below secured GSA noteholders, who are themselves under-recovered.
waterfall.residual_to_ordinary_shareholders_note: NIL under the base and bear scenarios. Gross realisations (NZ$4.7m) less assumed receivership/liquidation costs (NZ$0.6-1.5m, point estimate NZ$1.0m) leaves roughly NZ$3.7m against a NZ$2.53m secured claim alone - on the point estimate this technically clears the secured claim with headroom, which is why a token bull-case residual is modelled (see bull scenario) - but the receiver has explicitly and publicly reported the sale proceeds as INSUFFICIENT to fully repay secured noteholders, meaning either liquidation/receivership costs are running at or above the top of the assumed range, other secured-adjacent costs/claims not separately disclosed are consuming the gap, or the $4.7m headline figure nets differently than modelled here. Deferring to the receiver's own stated conclusion (proceeds insufficient for secured creditors) as the base and bear case, with the point-estimate arithmetic shown only as a transparency check, not overridden as the primary answer. Either way, unsecured creditors and ordinary shareholders are below a secured tier that is not being paid out in full, so the residual to equity is NIL in both base and bear.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Not applicable in the conventional sense. Only two audited fiscal years (FY2021, FY2022) exist in the Metrics.csv - no FY2023 or later audited accounts were ever filed, itself a cited reason for the Dec-2024 delisting. Shareholders' equity fell from NZ$17.06m (FY2021) to NZ$11.87m (FY2022), a -30.4% single-year decline. Free cash flow was deeply negative in both years on record (FY2021 -NZ$3.43m, FY2022 -NZ$5.70m, i.e. cash burn ACCELERATING, not stabilizing) against nominal revenue (FY2022 NZ$0.141m against a NZ$8.22m total loss). There is no positive, repeatable earnings or cash flow series to compound in any direction - this is precisely why a growth DCF is invalid here and a creditor-waterfall liquidation model is used instead.
historical_growth.notes: Historical FCF: FY2021 -NZ$3.434806m, FY2022 -NZ$5.70491m (Metrics.csv). Revenue was nominal in both years (FY2021 NZ$0.206m, FY2022 NZ$0.141m) against losses of NZ$3.12m and NZ$8.22m respectively - a structurally unviable unit-economics gap that was never closed before the company collapsed into administration in Mar-2024. Accumulated deficit reached NZ$17.4m at 31-Dec-2022. Approximately NZ$30 million of shareholder capital was raised and destroyed over the company's listed life; the Feb-2026 receivership asset sale realised only NZ$4.7m against that capital base, and even that sum was reported insufficient to fully repay the NZ$2.53m of secured debt ahead of equity.

base.narrative: Receivership proceeds to liquidation as the receiver has publicly stated. The Feb-2026 sale of operating subsidiaries for NZ$4.7m, net of receivership/liquidation costs, is insufficient to fully repay the NZ$2.53m secured GSA noteholder claim (per the receiver's own reporting). Unsecured creditors (NZ$0.109m) and ordinary shareholders rank below an already-underwater secured tier and recover nothing.
base.discounting_note: No cash flow stream exists to discount. This is a point-in-time creditor-priority waterfall on a fixed, already-realised asset pool (the Feb-2026 NZ$4.7m sale), not a projection.

bull.narrative: Speculative, low-probability residual-recovery scenario. Liquidators of another part of the group were reported to be disputing certain asset sales and related-party loans; if such a claw-back action succeeds AND assumed receivership/liquidation costs land at the low end of the range (NZ$0.6m) rather than the point estimate, there is a theoretical narrow path to fully repaying the NZ$2.53m secured claim and the NZ$0.109m unsecured claim with a small token surplus reaching ordinary equity. Explicitly labelled speculative: the receiver has already and publicly stated the confirmed NZ$4.7m sale proceeds are insufficient for secured creditors, so this scenario requires an ADDITIONAL, currently unquantified and unconfirmed recovery on top of the disclosed facts.

bear.narrative: Liquidation confirmed, exactly as the receiver has stated is expected. Secured GSA noteholders remain under-recovered even after the Feb-2026 asset sale; no further recoveries materialise for unsecured creditors or, a fortiori, for ordinary shareholders. Total loss of the ~NZ$30 million shareholders invested over the company's listed life.

base.note: No multi-year FCF projection exists or is modelled. This is a single point-in-time liquidation waterfall on the confirmed Feb-2026 NZ$4.7m asset sale, not a forward projection.

bull.note: See assumptions.bull for the speculative claw-back residual-recovery scenario. No cash flow projection is modelled.

bear.note: Liquidation confirmed; no cash flow projection is modelled.

base.methodology: Creditor-priority waterfall on the confirmed Feb-2026 NZ$4.7m subsidiary sale. The receiver has publicly reported these proceeds as insufficient to fully repay the NZ$2.53m secured GSA noteholder claim. Unsecured creditors and ordinary shareholders rank below an already-underwater secured tier. Residual to ordinary equity: NIL.

bull.methodology: Token, explicitly speculative residual-recovery case requiring (a) a successful liquidator claw-back of disputed related-party asset sales/loans generating an additional ~NZ$100k of recoveries, and (b) receivership/liquidation costs landing at the low end of the assumed range. Even under this favourable-tail scenario the per-share value is under NZ$0.001 (NZ$0.0007) - a rounding error, not an investment thesis. Assigned only 3% probability weight.

bear.methodology: Liquidation confirmed, receivership/liquidation costs at the top of the assumed range. Secured noteholders remain under-recovered; total loss for ordinary equity.

entry_price.rationale: There is no price at which CBD.NZ equity is investable. The 15%-IRR entry-price formula is undefined here: it requires a projected interim cash flow stream plus a fair-value exit, and this entity has neither - it is delisted (no functioning secondary market since 17-Dec-2024), in receivership, has no going-concern business, and the confirmed creditor waterfall places ordinary equity's expected residual at NIL under both the base and bear scenarios. Even the token bull-case residual (~NZ$0.0007/share, 3% probability) is not an actionable entry point - it is a rounding error attached to a low-probability contingent litigation outcome, not a tradeable security (there is no market maker, no NZX quote, and no confirmed off-market trading facility). Entry price is set to NZ$0.00 and should be read as 'uninvestable,' not as a buy signal at zero.

sensitivity.description: A standard WACC / terminal-growth sensitivity grid is not meaningful here - there is no perpetuity cash-flow stream to discount. Instead this matrix sensitizes the base-case waterfall residual to (rows) assumed receivership/liquidation costs and (columns) an additional speculative asset-recovery amount (e.g. from a successful liquidator claw-back), both layered on top of the confirmed NZ$4.7m gross realisation and the NZ$2.53m secured + NZ$0.109m unsecured claims.
sensitivity.matrix_read_note: Row = assumed receivership/liquidation costs (NZ$0.6m to NZ$1.5m). Column = additional speculative recovery beyond the confirmed NZ$4.7m sale (NZ$0 to NZ$1.0m). Cell = max(0, 4,700,000 + additional_recovery - receivership_costs - 2,530,000 - 109,000) / 140,435,616 shares. Only the top-right and bottom-right corners (low costs AND/OR large speculative recoveries) produce any positive per-share value at all, and even the most favourable modelled cell (NZ$0.0129/share) is a small fraction of the stale NZ$0.098 last-traded price. The receiver's own public statement that the confirmed NZ$4.7m sale was insufficient for secured creditors implies the true operating point sits at or below the zero-residual cells in this grid, consistent with the base and bear scenarios above.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear and base are together assigned 97% probability because the receiver has already publicly and specifically stated that the confirmed Feb-2026 NZ$4.7m asset sale proceeds are insufficient to fully repay the NZ$2.53m secured GSA noteholder claim - this is not a projection or a modelling assumption, it is a disclosed fact from the party administering the wind-down. Both bear and base scenarios independently conclude a NIL residual to ordinary equity (they differ only in assumed receivership/liquidation cost severity, which is immaterial to the equity outcome since the secured tier is already underwater in both). Bull (3%) reflects a narrow, explicitly speculative path requiring a successful liquidator claw-back of disputed related-party asset sales/loans on top of the already-disclosed shortfall - a real but unconfirmed and unquantified contingency mentioned in Feb-2026 reporting, assigned a low weight because no such recovery has been confirmed and the base fact pattern (secured creditors already under-recovered) works directly against it.

sanity_check.diagnosis: Standard implied-multiple sanity checks (P/E, EV/EBITDA, P/B versus peers) are NOT APPLICABLE and are deliberately not fabricated here: Cannasouth has no going-concern business, no positive earnings, no EBITDA, no audited accounts since FY2022, and no market price (the entity has been delisted since 17-Dec-2024 with the last trade a stale, non-transactable artifact). The relevant sanity check for a receivership/liquidation valuation is instead whether the waterfall residual to equity is consistent with the receiver's own public disclosures - it is: the receiver has explicitly stated the confirmed NZ$4.7m Feb-2026 asset sale is insufficient to fully repay the NZ$2.53m secured GSA noteholder claim, which mechanically and necessarily means unsecured creditors (NZ$0.109m) and ordinary shareholders (last in priority) recover nothing. A weighted intrinsic value of ~NZ$0.0000/share is not an overly pessimistic model output requiring a fix - it is the correct arithmetic consequence of a disclosed, under-recovered secured-creditor shortfall, and the model passes because it does not manufacture a positive valuation the facts do not support.
sanity_check.fix_applied: none required - liquidation_waterfall method applied instead of growth DCF, consistent with a receivership entity with a confirmed secured-creditor shortfall and no going-concern business

valuation_philosophy.why_dcf_was_rejected: A discounted-cash-flow model requires a repeatable, positive forward free-cash-flow stream and a defensible terminal value to capitalize into perpetuity. Cannasouth has neither: it produced deeply negative free cash flow in every audited year on record (FY2021 -NZ$3.43m, FY2022 -NZ$5.70m) against nominal revenue, filed no audited accounts after FY2022, entered voluntary administration in Mar-2024, was delisted from the NZX in Dec-2024, and has been in receivership since May-2025 with the receiver publicly stating liquidation is the expected outcome. Its operating subsidiaries - the only assets that could ever have generated future cash flow - were sold out of the listed entity entirely in Feb-2026 to a new private owner (Marshall Road Holdings) for NZ$4.7 million, a sum the receiver has already reported as insufficient even to repay the NZ$2.53 million owed to secured noteholders ahead of ordinary shareholders. Projecting growth, margins, or a terminal multiple onto a company with no remaining operating assets, no going-concern status, and a confirmed secured-creditor shortfall would not be conservative accounting for uncertainty - it would be modelling a business that no longer exists inside the listed vehicle. The only analytically honest approach for an insolvent entity in active receivership is a creditor-priority liquidation waterfall applied to the actual, disclosed realisation.
valuation_philosophy.conclusion: Ordinary equity in Cannasouth Limited (CBD.NZ) is worthless. The confirmed Feb-2026 sale of its operating subsidiaries for NZ$4.7 million has already been reported by the receiver as insufficient to fully repay the NZ$2.53 million owed to secured GSA noteholders, a claim that ranks ahead of the NZ$0.109 million owed to unsecured creditors, which in turn ranks ahead of ordinary shareholders at the bottom of the priority stack. Under the base and bear scenarios (97% combined probability weight) the residual to equity is NIL. Even the narrow, explicitly speculative bull scenario (3% probability, contingent on an unconfirmed liquidator claw-back of disputed related-party transactions) implies a per-share value of roughly NZ$0.0007 - a rounding error against the stale NZ$0.098 last-traded price, not an investment thesis. Approximately NZ$30 million of shareholder capital raised over the company's listed life has been destroyed. The probability-weighted intrinsic value is NZ$0.0000/share.
